title: Assigning NULL to a cache_mem() object corrupts the data
description:
Calling `m$set("key", NULL)` does not correctly assign NULL to that key, but instead deletes the entry from the underlying list. However, instead of that key being missing, all elements after it in the underlying lists get moved forward by one, so `m$get()` returns the wrong result not only for that key but for all keys that were inserted after it.

See detailed reprex below. I will submit a pull request momentarily with a fix.

``` r
library(cachem)

# NULL assignment corrupts data with cache_mem()
m <- cache_mem()
m$set("a", 1)
m$set("b", 2)
m$set("c", 3)
m$set("d", 4)

m$set("b", NULL)

m$get("a")   #> 1
#> [1] 1
m$get("b")   #> 3      ← wrong, should be NULL
#> [1] 3
m$get("c")   #> 4      ← wrong, should be 3
#> [1] 4
m$get("d")   #> NULL   ← wrong, should be 4
#> NULL
m$get("e")   #> <Key Missing>
#> <Key Missing>


# NULL assignment works correctly with cache_disk()
d <- cache_disk(tempfile())
d$set("a", 1)
d$set("b", 2)
d$set("c", 3)
d$set("d", 4)

d$set("b", NULL)

d$get("a")
#> [1] 1
d$get("b")
#> NULL
d$get("c")
#> [1] 3
d$get("d")
#> [1] 4
d$get("e")
#> <Key Missing>

packageVersion("cachem")
#> [1] '1.1.0'
```

title: FR: $age() or $ttl()
description:
There are times with some caches where I want to "peek" ahead and, if the TTL of an expiring object is "soon" (contextual) then try to repopulate the object and therefore update the data or at least extend its expiration. Unfortunately, the only way I know I'm "near expiration" atm is to expire, at which point I lose the object and cannot extend.

The issue is that the mechanism for getting the data to cache is not infallible, and failure does not mean I want to dump the data.

For instance, if I have a cache that expires every day, I may choose to reattempt to update/extend the object if I'm within an hour of expiration, that way if the acquisition method fails, I still have (up to) an hour before it goes away.

title: Feature Request | Cache to SQL Database
With `cache_disk`, using `max_age` together with `evict="lru"` may not work correctly
description:
When `evict="lru"` is used, it calls `Sys.setFileTime()` to update the file's mtime, instead of relying on filesystem access modifying the atime. This is because atime is not reliable across platforms, and on some platforms has very low resolution.

However, this can cause problems when using `max_age`, because `max_age` is supposed to be the time since the file was created. In other words, `evict="lru"` is supposed to use the last access time, but `max_age` is supposed to use the file creation time; however we currently only use the `mtime` for time information.

This is the behavior without using `get()` to fetch an object. The cache is created with a `max_age` of 2 seconds. As expected, the object is pruned from the cache by the end, after 2.1 seconds have passed:

```R
library(cachem)
dc <- cache_disk(max_age = 2, evict = "lru")
dc$set("a", 123)

Sys.sleep(1)
dc$prune()
dc$keys()
#> [1] "a"

Sys.sleep(1.1)
dc$prune()
dc$keys()
#> character(0)
```


However, if `get()` is called on the key, it causes the key to persist longer than 2 seconds:

```R
library(cachem)
dc <- cache_disk(max_age = 2, evict = "lru")
dc$set("a", 123)

Sys.sleep(1)
dc$prune()
dc$keys()
#> [1] "a"

dc$get("a")
#> [1] 123

Sys.sleep(1.1)
dc$prune()
dc$keys()
#> [1] "a"
```


It might be possible to use `ctime`, but we'll need to make sure it behaves reliably across platforms, and with decent time resolution.

title: Possible reasons of cache file not being written
description:
Hello, thank you for this package. It is really useful. 

I am using this package and it creates cache file for every possible scenario except for one. I am trying to figure out why but I don't understand. I cannot share a reproducible example but I will give a gist for you to get an idea. 

```
cd <- cachem::cache_disk(d,
                             read_fn = qs::qread,
                             write_fn = qs::qsave,
                             extension = ".qs",
                             evict = "lru",
                             logfile = fs::path(d, "log", ext = "txt"),
                             prune_rate = 50)

fun1 <- memoise::memoise(fun1, cache = cd, omit_args = "lkup")

# This works and creates the cache file
fun1(country = "IND", year = "all")
# This too creates the file
fun1(country = "all", year = 2017)
# However, this does not and I don't know why
fun1(country = "all", year = "all")
```

I have thought about the size of the file generated since country = "all" and year = "all" generates a lot of data but in RStudio Environment Window I see it as 33 MB which I think is not a lot (?) to avoid creating the cache file. 

Another thing that I noticed is the `logfile` is not being written at all. I am not sure if I am using it incorrectly here. 

Any idea why in this one particular case of country = "all" and year = "all" cache file is not generated?

title: assignment operator request
description:
Hi would you consider adding another method to cache_disk? Currently I have:
```r
cache <- cache_disk()

`%<-%` <- function(n, v) {
        n_str <- deparse(substitute(n))
        if (!cache$exists(n_str)) cache$set(n_str, v)
        assign(n_str, cache$get(n_str), envir=parent.frame())
}
```
I just change `<-` to `%<-%` when I want it cached.

I would prefer if cachem make one of the following options do the same thing:
```r
# option A
`%<-%` <- cache_disk()
# B
cache <- cache_disk()
`%<-%` <- cache$assign_op
# C
cache <- cache_disk(assign_op = "%<-%")
```
I think A looks the best but I don't see how it can be done while still allowing `cache$set` etc. in existing code.

title: Isolate random seed for cachem
description:
It is a widespread practice to rely on `set.seed()` to construct pseudo-random sets of analyses, but in a reproducible manner.

Some functions within the `cachem` package modify this seed, but it is not obvious to users of the package that they should do so. This can (and did in my case) lead to unexpected and hard to debug behavior when cachem is introduced into such analysis directly or through intermediate packages that rely on `cachem` for its effectiveness as a caching library.

The issue can be demonstrated with a simple reprex:

``` r
library(cachem)
library(testthat)
cm <- cache_mem()
cd <- cache_disk(tempdir())

set.seed(42)
expect_equal(sample(99999, 1), 61413)

set.seed(42)
cm$set("x",letters)
expect_equal(sample(99999, 1), 61413)

set.seed(42)
cd$set("x",letters)
expect_equal(sample(99999, 1), 61413)
#> Error: sample(99999, 1) not equal to 61413.
#> 1/1 mismatches
#> [1] 73236 - 61413 == 11823
```

The above also demonstrates that seed updates depend on the type of the cache, which can further complicate things (something that works with a memory cache can stop working when switching to a layered or disk cache).

My suggested fix would be to isolate the usage of the random seed wherever `cachem` needs access to randomness, so that the global seed is not affected by calls to `cachem` functions.

A discussion of this issue can be found here:
* https://stackoverflow.com/questions/23090958/isolate-randomness-of-a-local-environment-from-the-global-r-process

And an implementation of this within the `shiny` package (which is the approach I would recommend) can be found here:
* https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/434/files

I'd be happy to discuss the best approach to this fix/enhancement, and provide an eventual pull request if it seems like it would be well-received.

title: With custom missing keys layered cache never gets objects beyond first layer
description:

title: per-element max_age?
description:
Is it realistic (do you see other justification/rationale) to allow per-`key` max_age?

As an example, I'm querying an API for weekend schedules. The schedules tend to change very slowly in general, but approaching one week out they tend to change much more quickly. A weekend's schedule is pulled all at one time, so I'd like to be able to support a longer max-age for weekends further out, but within (say) 10 days, the values expire more quickly.

I'm querying and using through the end of the year, and I don't want to query every weekend multiple times a day; however, I want to query for *this* weekend every few hours.

I know that the `max_age` is cache-specific, is there a way to fake this, or do you see another mechanism for supporting this short of assigning to difference `cache_*` instances? `cache_layer` by itself won't work, I suspect, without a bit more work. (Or maybe it will, and I haven't figured it out yet.)

For instance, if it is just "this weekend" and "not this weekend", I could create

```r
soon <- cache_mem(max_age = 3600)     # hourly
notsoon <- cache_mem(max_age = 86400) # daily
thisweekend <- "2021-07-09"
shouldbesoon <- as.numeric(as.Date(thisweekend) - Sys.Date(), units = "days") < 10

if (shouldbesoon) {
  value <- soon$get(thisweekend)
  if (is.key_missing(value)) {
    value <- update_my_data(thisweekend)
    soon$set(thisweekend, value)
  }
  notsoon$remove(thisweekend)
} else {
  value <- soon$get(thisweekend)
  if (is.key_missing(value)) {
    value <- update_my_data(thisweekend)
    notsoon$set(thisweekend, value)
  }
}
```

If `$set()` supported its own `max_age`, then this could be replaced with

```r
cch <- cache_mem(max_age=86400) # default for most objects
thisweekend <- "2021-07-09"

value <- cch$get(thisweekend)
if (is.key_missing(value)) {
  value <- update_my_data(thisweekend)
  cch$set(thisweekend, value, max_age = expire)
  expire <- if (as.numeric(as.Date(thisweekend) - Sys.Date(), units = "days") < 10) 3600 else 86400
}
```

There can be cause to have a third tier, which is why I'm asking if there is a better way to address this.

title: Understanding cache pruning
description:
I'm trying to understand how pruning works. My goal is to use it for a shiny app on shinyapps.io. I'd like certain objects to be cached and shared by multiple users. Of course, I'm aware that shinyapps.io doesn't have persistent storage, but I'm happy with that as I actually want `max_age` not to be `Inf`. 24 hours is probably the maximum I would go with.

```
app_cache <- cachem::cache_disk(file.path(dirname(tempdir()), "my-app"), max_age = 10)
shinyOptions(cache = app_cache)
# my app here
```
With this, the rds file in `temp/my-app` is not actually deleted after 10 seconds. If I understand correctly pruning only occurs at least every 20 minutes and something needs to trigger `set()` another time before the file is deleted. 

So for example
12:00:00 - User 1 uses the app (`foo.rds` is cached)
12:00:05 - User 2 uses the app and benefits from caching
12:00:10 - `foo.rds` expires but still exists in `temp/my-app`
12:20:00 - User 3 uses the app (`set()` triggers `prune()` which deletes `foo.rds`), User 3 doesn't benefit from caching

Am I understanding this correctly?

title: Speed up `set()` resp. `prune()`
description:
I use `memoise()` to cache requests to an API. As the API is relatively fast I noticed how over time it got slower and slower. After some digging I found that quite a bit of time is spend in `prune()` which is called every time in `set()`.
For longer running functions the overhead is relatively small but for fast ones it would be great to make this a bit more efficient.

Code to replicate

```r
f <- function(x) {
  x
}

f_mem <- memoise::memoise(f)

purrr::walk(1:10e3, f_mem)

profvis::profvis({purrr::walk(10e3 + 1:1e3, f_mem)})
```
